subQuestions.questionText:
The difference between jet lag and jet fatigue:
A Jet lag is travel between two cities within a country and jet fatigue is travel between two cities in a neighbouring country.
B Jet lag is tiredness due to crossing many time zones and jet fatigue is tiredness due to a long-haul flight.
C Jet lag is stress on an aircraft caused by wind speed and jet fatigue is exhaustion during a flight due to the age of the plane.
D Jet lag has limited or no side effects on passengers, while jet fatigue has many symptoms and may require hospitalisation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
Jet lag is tiredness due to crossing many time zones, while jet fatigue is tiredness due to a long-haul flight.

options.A: Jet lag is travel between two cities within a country and jet fatigue is travel between two cities in a neighbouring country.
options.B: Jet lag is tiredness due to crossing many time zones and jet fatigue is tiredness due to a long-haul flight.
options.C: Jet lag is stress on an aircraft caused by wind speed and jet fatigue is exhaustion during a flight due to the age of the plane.
options.D: Jet lag has limited or no side effects on passengers, while jet fatigue has many symptoms and may require hospitalisation.

subQuestions.questionText: Read the information about the launch of a global Covid-19 passport for tourism. Do you think the global Covid-19 passport will restore international travel? Give TWO reasons for your opinion.

YES:
• Destination countries can now safely re-open their borders for inbound international tourists without fear of mass COVID-19 transmission.
• Reduce the strain on the health care system of the destination country.
• Will promote freedom of movement without fear of infection and transmission.
• Promote international travel because of widespread vaccination programmes and campaigns.

OR

NO:
• Tourists who do not want to be vaccinated will not be able to travel internationally.
• The requirement of a COVID-19 passport for international travel can be regarded as discrimination and infringement on human rights.
• Tourists may not want to get vaccinated because there may be a misconception that it is a fraudulent exercise.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss TWO ways in which UNESCO is involved in the declaration of World Heritage Sites.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each way discussed (max 4 marks):
• Gives feedback and suggestions to improve nomination information in the file.
• Visits and evaluates the site for its universal value.
• Meets as a committee to discuss findings and make decisions.
• Announces newly-declared World Heritage Sites and adds these sites to the list on their website.
• Regular on-site inspections to ensure standards are being maintained.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ONE reason why the golden rhino is significant. (Refer to the Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape picture in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE reason:
• The golden rhino is an item crafted by the ancient Mapungubwe civilisation.
• It symbolises gold and other trade the Mapungubwe people had with other parts of the world.
• The golden rhino was buried with the king, showing a civilisation with a social structure.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ONE reason why the hut made by the Nama people is significant. (Refer to the Richtersveld Cultural and Botanical Landscape picture in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE reason:
• The Nama people were nomadic (moved around seasonally), moving their housing with them.
• It is part of the past lifestyle and oral traditions of the Nama people that is still practised and protected.
• The mats used to build the huts help to regulate the intense heat that is experienced in the area.

subQuestions.questionText: Name the host country of the ITB Berlin.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer (2 marks): Germany

subQuestions.questionText: From the information above, give ONE reason why SATourism participated in ITB Berlin 2022.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE reason:
• Market South Africa as a destination of choice.
• Position South Africa as a safe, affordable, value-for-money destination.
• Exhibitions to showcase South Africa's tourism offerings to over 180 countries.
• Give small tourism businesses and emerging entrepreneurs the opportunity to market internationally.
• Represent South Africa's tourism businesses and organisations.
• Network with tourism professionals and key players from the global tourism industry.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss ONE way in which SATourism would have ensured that there was a geographic spread of South African product owners at ITB Berlin.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE way discussed:
• The tourism businesses that attended the ITB are from across all nine provinces in South Africa.
• Representation of South Africa's uniqueness and cultural diversity are from all areas in South Africa.
• Marketing benefits will flow to all nine provinces of South Africa.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ONE reason why the South African brand logo pictured above was displayed at all 50 tourism exhibitions at ITB Berlin 2022.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE reason:
• Increasing recognition of South Africa as a tourism destination and the packages on offer.
• Coordinating the various tourism products and offerings under one familiar banner.
• Always ready to reinvent and reignite the South African tourism industry.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss TWO ways in which the unacceptable appearance of employees at work can negatively impact business profitability.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each way discussed (max 4 marks):
• The customers will take their business elsewhere because they do not trust the image portrayed by the workers.
• The employee mirrors the image of the business, so the appearance creates customer perceptions that will not meet their expectations.
• Due to customers' negative perception of the tourism business, the customer may decide to scale down on their business transactions with the company.

subQuestions.questionText: Read the statement below: 'A job applicant should change his/her normal appearance when going for an interview and align his/her appearance to the company's profile.' Justify TWO points which reflect your opinion on the statement above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each point justified (max 4 marks). NOTE: Accept well-motivated answers that reflect a willingness to adhere to the company's profile/policies OR express a need for individuality.

AGREE/YES:
• The interviewers will be able to see how serious/committed this applicant is to get the job.
• The interviewers will see if the person will fit into the profile of the company.
• The applicant will show respect for the company's profile and policies, even before he/she is appointed.

OR

DISAGREE/NO:
• The applicant has freedom of expression and can dress anyway they want.
• The company's dress code must be flexible enough to allow for any expression of individuality.
• If the company does not like the appearance of the applicant, he/she has the right to decide whether or not to work for the company.

subQuestions.questionText: Josephine, a young entrepreneur, is planning to start a beauty salon. Respond to her question: Why should my business have a logo?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE answer:
• Josephine should have a logo designed that will convey a professional image for the beauty salon.
• Josephine must decide on the focus or theme of her beauty salon which should be reflected in the logo.
• As the business grows and becomes popular/recognisable, the logo will be associated with the beauty salon.

subQuestions.questionText: Respond to Josephine's question: What factors must I consider when choosing the name of my business?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE answer:
• Josephine should select an appropriate name for the spa which makes sense to the customers.
• The name should be easy to remember and must say something about the business.

subQuestions.questionText: Write down ONE word from the title 'HAKATOURS DIG DEEP INTO OUR ROOTS' that refers to both the environment and the community.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
• Roots
• Hakatours

subQuestions.questionText: Explain what Hakatours mean by practising 'the triple bottom line'.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for an explanation:
• A way of doing business in tourism that impacts positively on people, profitability of the business and the planet.
• A way of doing business in tourism that impacts positively on communities (societies), on the economy and on the environment.

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons why Hakatours only allow the planting of indigenous trees.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each reason (max 4 marks):
• Alien species are usually water-intense and will need more water than indigenous species.
• Indigenous species are better adapted to local climate and environment and will grow better.
• Planting indigenous trees is part of their sustainable practices on the farm.
• Alien species are invasive and impact negatively on the growth of endemic (indigenous) plants, and are therefore removed rather than planted.

subQuestions.questionText: Write down THREE of Hakatours' sustainable activities and match ONE of the three pillars of the triple bottom-line approach to EACH.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each correct activity-pillar pairing (3 × 2 = 6 marks). NOTE: Accept reference made to the Hakatours' website.
• Planting of indigenous trees → Environmental (planet) pillar
• Use of local photographers → Social (people) pillar
• Creating entrepreneurship opportunities for locals → Social (people) pillar / Financial / Economic (profit/money) pillar
• Responsible use of wood for photo frames → Environmental (planet) pillar

subQuestions.questionText: Scotland is part of the United Kingdom. Choose TWO other countries that also form part of the UK from the following: England, Greece, Ireland, Wales.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each (max 2 marks). Accept any TWO of:
• England
• Wales
• Ireland

NOTE: While Northern Ireland is part of the UK, the memo accepts 'Ireland' as the listed answer.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss TWO advantages of Scotland hosting COP26 for the neighbouring countries chosen in QUESTION 9.1.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each advantage discussed (max 4 marks):
• Delegates from other parts of the world extended their stay and visited the neighbouring countries.
• These countries also benefited financially from the COP26 in Scotland when delegates spent money in their countries.
• The neighbouring countries may have focused their marketing on the delegates by making special packages available to them.
• These countries received free exposure and publicity because delegates posted photos of their visits on Instagram and other social media platforms.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain TWO reasons why the youth was involved in COP26 through the Milan gathering in September.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each reason explained (max 4 marks):
• The youth are the decision-makers on climate change of the future. Their inputs are invaluable.
• The youth are the future generation who will be living with the decisions made now and should be part of the decision-making process.
• The youth may have a fresh approach to climate change and innovative ideas on how to bring the message across to their generation.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain TWO reasons why the Covid-19 pandemic is regarded as the main reason for postponing the conference in 2020.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each reason explained (max 4 marks):
• Global travel restrictions were in place in 2020 to limit the spread of the COVID-19 virus. Delegates from other parts of the world could not travel.
• Attendance numbers were restricted during various levels of lockdown.
• The use of digital platforms became an alternative for physical meetings during the COVID-19 period. Some planning meetings went ahead despite lockdown regulations worldwide.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain THREE ways in which the organisers had to ensure the protection of all delegates against Covid-19 at COP26 in 2021.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each way explained (max 6 marks). NOTE: Accept details of safety protocols.
• All delegates had to adhere to COVID-19 safety protocols, e.g. social distancing, hand washing, wearing of masks etc.
• Special arrangements had to be made for meals/drinks to comply with regulations pertaining to the capacity of venues.
• Regular sanitation of venues, vehicles and hotel rooms.
• Awareness across all venues to comply with COVID-19 safety protocols.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the type of technology for payment common in ALL the pictures above. (Refer to the Paying for Goods and Services in Glasgow images in the question paper showing card readers, cellphones, and smartwatches.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for any ONE. Accept EFT (Electronic Funds Transfer):
• Digital payments
• Electronic payments
• Online payments
• Cellphone payments

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE disadvantage of using this type of technology in QUESTION 9.3.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE disadvantage. Accept disadvantages of using a cellphone to make payments:
• All the technology above is dependent on internet connectivity.
• If there is no internet connectivity, no transaction will go through immediately.
• With device/electricity failure no transactions can be processed.

subQuestions.questionText: Apart from the technology in the pictures above, suggest TWO ways in which customers at COP26 can pay for goods and services.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for each way (max 2 marks):
• Pre-paid debit cards
• Credit Cards
• Cash

subQuestions.questionText: As the manager of a hotel, select the level of customer satisfaction from Picture 1 you would like to see most often in feedback from guests. (Refer to Picture 1 showing five satisfaction levels A–E from very unhappy to very happy in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for any ONE:
• E
• D

(Both represent positive/happy customer satisfaction levels.)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason for your answer to QUESTION 10.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE reason:
• If all customers are completely satisfied with all aspects of the hotel, the manager will know they are doing everything right.
• The guests are completely satisfied with the level of service they receive from the staff.
• It can lead to positive word-of-mouth.

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to Picture 2. Explain ONE way in which managers can use the feedback from customers to the advantage of the hotel.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE way explained:
• Comments and complaints from individual guests can reveal problems managers may not have been aware of.
• Customer feedback can be a barometer for what a hotel does right.
• Managers are advised to tap into customer feedback as often as possible to plan intervention activities.
• Hotels depend on honest customer feedback in order to know which practices improve guest satisfaction and which need to be re-evaluated.
